SOCOM history identifies the 8 October 1987 firefight at Middle Shoals Buoy. The US counter-memorial paragraph 1.50 supports the event near Farsi Island; map 1.6 (PDFpage 35) explicitly labels the buoy with a latitude/longitude graticule, but was prepared to show the 24 July Bridgeton mining and provides no numeric coordinates for the buoy itself. It is a litigant map, not a Court finding. No coordinate has been read to false precision or borrowed from Farsi Island. The closer new lead is the contemporary CENTCOM9 October 1987 cable, Exhibit 78, cited by paragraph 1.50.

sources.label: US Special Operations Command history, Operation Earnest Will, hosted by National Security Archive, PDFpage 16
ICJ Oil Platforms case: US counter-memorial and counter-claim, 23 June 1997, para 1.50/map 1.6 (PDFpages 52/35)
National Defense University, Joint Force Quarterly 29, Joint Special Operations in Support of Earnest Will, First Blood section

records.nextEvidenceNeeded: Inspect Exhibit 78 or a dated hydrographic buoy listing before assigning a numeric point. Approximate map interpolation was not promoted in this bounded pass.

records.finding: Original event coordinate [138.834, -1.195] is offshore. The official Army history explicitly places the battle at the named coral hill on Maffin Bay, west of the Snaky River and east of Maffin Airfield. Maps 11 andIV were visually inspected: tactical geometry, scale and the hill are present, but there is no latitude/longitude graticule. Do not simply transpose latitude digits to -1.95 or use the bay centroid. A georeferenced military topo sheet or official terrain control points remain necessary.

sources.label: US Army Center of Military History, The Approach to the Philippines, chapter X and map 11; primary official history reproduced by HyperWar/ibiblio
US Army official history, chapter XI and mapIV, Lone Tree Hill
Army University Press, Lone Tree Hill virtual staff ride

records.nextEvidenceNeeded: Georeferenced original tactical/topographic map or institutionally surveyed hill coordinate.

The Navy places the engagement off Pacocha on 29 May 1877. The 1877 Astete/Carrasco combat plan preserved by BnF plots individual ship movements near Ilo, Pacocha and Punta de Coles; the full image was inspected. It has a distance scale and bearings but no coordinate graticule. The shore village or modern municipal center cannot substitute for the plotted offshore action. No coordinate has been inferred from the drawing.

sources.label: Peruvian Navy official history: naval action off Pacocha on 29 May 1877
BnF GED-2193, Astete/Carrasco, Plano de Pacocha y del combate, 17 September 1877
Revista de Marina, 2019 no.2, John Rodríguez Asti, El combate naval de Pacocha, pp 80–93

records.nextEvidenceNeeded: Independent georeferenced chart/control points for the 1877 plan, or a contemporary log with an engagement position.

records.finding: Wilkes primary narrative identifies Utiroa as the attacked and burned village. That is a useful specific location identity; the cached event point [174.8, 1.35] does not itself establish it. No contemporary georeferenced village point was inspected; neither reversing latitude sign nor using the whole atoll centroid is approved.

NHHC confirms the naval engagement on 2 July 1950 off the east coast of Korea, not far south of the 38 thparallel. This locates an area, not an exact battlefield point. It is insufficient to turn the rejected Sea of Japan place centroid into an accepted coordinate. The narrative also has a stray June/July month typo; its heading establishes the July event, and this audit proposes no date change.

sources.label: US Naval History and Heritage Command, H-050-1, Battle of Chumonchin Chan section

records.nextEvidenceNeeded: Juneau/Jamaica/Black Swan action report or log position for 2 July 1950.
